subject: Channel-strip send slots: the slot's own menu mark, and what appears once a send is assigned
question: Does anything at the SOURCE report which destination a send slot holds?

reverify.expected: With no send assigned, exactly one item is marked and it is the no-send entry.

method: The probe gained `--marks`, which reads `AXMenuItemMarkChar` on every item of the opened slot menu, and `--slot-index`, because a strip shows more than one send slot once one is assigned and `first` then answers about whichever the tree orders first. Readings were taken with no send assigned, then after selecting `Bus 12` by title, then after Edit > Undo. The assignment was confirmed from Logic's own undo entry, not from the slot, because the slot's readback is the thing in question.

observations.what: menu marks with no send assigned
observations.title: No Send

observations.what: Logic's undo entry after selecting Bus 12
observations.title: Undo Change Send in Channel Strip

observations.what: a Send Level control in the tree, before the assignment
a Send Level control in the tree, after the assignment
the right inspector strip after the assignment
observations.note: the DESTINATION aux, not the sending strip

observations.what: send slots carrying the `Send slot.` help prefix, after the assignment
menu marks read after the assignment, on the slot the probe opens
observations.title: No Send

conclusion: A send slot's menu DOES mark its current choice — with nothing assigned, exactly one item is marked and it is the no-send entry. That is a readback surface the earlier reading never opened, and it needs no mapping between the strip's spelling and the menu's. Separately, a Send Level slider EXISTS only once a send is assigned, which answers the earlier record's open question about that control: its presence reports that the slot holds a send, though not which destination.
limits: It is NOT established that the mark follows an assignment. After assigning `Bus 12` the mark read on the opened slot was still the no-send entry — and the strip grew from one send slot to three, so the slot the probe opened is very likely an EMPTY one rather than the assigned one. The next measurement has to open the menu of the slot that owns the send, which the tree identifies as the `send button` immediately preceding the `send knob`. Until that is done this is an untested candidate, not a working readback.

The assignment itself is established only from Logic's undo entry and from two side effects — the Send Level slider appearing and the right inspector strip becoming the destination aux. None of those is the source-side readback this ADR needs.
One send, one strip, one project. The menu titles are localised and an implementation must go through AXLocalePolicy; `No Send` is this host's spelling, not a constant.
The probe moves the strip's Mute control as part of its protocol and the extra send slots disappeared between runs, so back-to-back invocations are not reading an unchanged strip.
